location.evidence: Three of the lowest-paying programs are campuses in Puerto Rico. Pay on the island is well below the mainland in every major occupational group.

prestige.evidence: The top programs admit far fewer applicants than is typical for the major, and schools like Michigan Ross send most graduates to banks and consulting firms. Some other top programs are open-admission degrees for working adults.

stepping_stone.evidence: Most business graduates go straight to work. The usual graduate degree is an MBA, and most MBA students wait several years after their bachelor's degree before they enroll.

programs.evidence: Bismarck State's online Energy Management bachelor's requires an applied associate degree or energy training before admission. It is built for people already working in the energy industry who want to become supervisors or managers.
Michigan's Ross School of Business is highly selective. Nearly all of its business graduates get job offers, mostly from financial services and consulting firms such as McKinsey and Goldman Sachs.
City University of Seattle offers its business degree online as a degree-completion program for working adults and transfer students.
